newsitem.title: NORWAY: Perky Oslo bourse climbs to new record high.
newsitem.headline: Perky Oslo bourse climbs to new record high.

text.p: The Oslo bourse set a new all-time high for the second consecutive day on Thursday, helped by positive financial results in Orkla and Saga Petroleum and a recovery in high-technology stock Nera.
The Total share index hit a peak at 856.66 points before settling back to close at 855.77 points, a rise of 0.15 percent. Turnover was a perky 851 million crowns.
Food and beverage-based conglomerate Orkla climbed steeply after posting a 26 percent surge in pre-tax profits in the first eight months to 1.75 billion crowns.
Orkla hit a new life high at 374 crowns before ending eight crowns up at 373 crowns in 64.3 million crowns of business.
"The results were very positive for Orkla. They made gains on their share portfolio and the positive sentiment in the market today only helps their portfolio more," said one dealer.
"In the long term I'm positive, but short term I think it will be two steps forward and one back for Orkla."

Telecommunications group Nera added a hefty eight crowns to 227 crowns in 54.6 million crowns of trade. Brokers said the rise was partly a recovery from recent losses and partly due to good recommendations by international brokerages.
